name: Why is there water around the base of my toilet?

mainEntity.name: Why is there water around the base of my toilet?

acceptedAnswer.text: Water around the base of your toilet can stem from several issues, including a loose toilet or a compromised wax ring seal. A crack in the porcelain bowl or tank could also be the culprit. Leaks can also originate from the fill valve inside the tank, the supply line connection, or a clogged drain causing overflow. Identifying the exact source quickly is crucial to prevent further water damage to your flooring and subfloor. If the water appears only when flushing, it's often a wax ring or flange issue.
acceptedAnswer.description: Water around your toilet's base usually indicates a leak from the wax ring, a loose toilet, a cracked bowl, or a faulty supply line. Prompt identification is important to prevent further damage.
